guide.description: -vf scale=W:H resizes video to a target width and height in pixels. It's how a raw high-resolution export gets turned into a smaller version for the web, e.g. downscaling a 1080p source to 720p or 360p. It combines with -ss/-t (covered in the previous lesson) to both resize and trim a clip in the same call.

flags.desc: resize video to width W, height H

examples.note: resize AND trim in one call

exercises.title: Resize a video
exercises.task: Convert raw-interview.mov to interview-720p.mp4, scaled to 1280:720.
hints: -vf scale=<width>:<height> goes between -i <input> and the output file

exercises.title: A smaller target resolution
exercises.task: Convert raw-interview.mov to small.mp4, scaled all the way down to 640:360.
hints: Same flag, a different width and height

exercises.title: Scale and trim together
exercises.task: Convert raw-interview.mov to clip360.mp4: scale it to 640:360, skip the first 30 seconds, and keep the next 60.
hints: -vf, -ss, and -t can all appear in the same call

exercises.title: Put it together: scale, then verify with ffprobe
exercises.task: Convert raw-interview.mov to clip720.mp4, scaled to 1280:720, then run ffprobe on clip720.mp4 to confirm the resolution.
hints: Convert first, then run ffprobe on the new file
ffmpeg -i raw-interview.mov -vf scale=1280:720 clip720.mp4, then ffprobe clip720.mp4
